title: Speaking Part 1 Short Extensions
content: Part 1 answers should be natural and not too long. Give a direct answer, then add one reason or example. A common mistake is answering with only yes or no, which gives too little language for the examiner to assess.

title: Speaking Part 2 Cue Card
content: In Part 2, use the one-minute preparation time to note people, place, time, reason, and feeling. Aim to speak for about 1 to 2 minutes. If you run out of ideas, add background, a comparison, or a personal reaction.

title: Speaking Part 3 Abstract Answers
content: Part 3 asks broader questions. Use a clear opinion, explanation, example, and short contrast if useful. Avoid only telling personal stories; connect your answer to society, education, technology, culture, or long-term effects.
